title: Read, Sign, Repeat

briefing.headline: GMP training in pharma: what you should know before the call
points: Sterile injectables plant, regulated under Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP). Every task an operator performs must be covered by a documented, effective training.
'Read and sign' means an operator reads the procedure (SOP) and signs that they understood it. It is cheap and auditable; whether it works is another question.
Deviations are recorded quality events. Each one needs an investigation and a corrective and preventive action (CAPA), and repeated deviations draw inspectors' attention.
The Belgian medicines agency (FAMHP) inspects the site; Quality Assurance (QA) must approve anything that counts as GMP training.

stakeholder.name: Dr. Nathalie Dubois
stakeholder.org: Vespera Pharma, a sterile injectables plant near Wavre with 650 staff
stakeholder.voice: Exact, calm, slightly formal; thinks in deviations, CAPAs and inspection readiness. Bilingual French and English. Dry, under-the-breath humour about paperwork. Appreciates precise questions.

opening_message: We've had a run of deviations on aseptic interventions. The CAPA says 'retrain operators'. I need all 140 cleanroom operators to re-read and sign the 23 relevant SOPs within the month, with a quiz. Can L&D set that up in the system?
surface_ask: Read-and-sign retraining on 23 SOPs plus a quiz for all 140 cleanroom operators.

gold.real_problem: The deviations come almost entirely from the new isolator line, from operators who joined in the last eight months. They were qualified by read-and-sign only, because the experienced trainer who did hands-on coaching left and was never replaced. The intervention SOP was rewritten into a 41-page document, and the glove-port technique can't be learned from paper.
gold.need_statement: New operators on the isolator line lack the hands-on skill for aseptic interventions. They need practical training and observed qualification on a mock-up or during line downtime, and the SOP needs a usable one-page visual. Re-reading 23 SOPs for all 140 operators adds paperwork without adding skill.

hidden_facts.fact: Fourteen of the 16 deviations happened on the new isolator line; the two older lines are almost clean.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks where, on which line or in which area the deviations occur.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: Fourteen of the sixteen are on Line 4, the new isolator. Lines 1 and 2 are practically boring. I like boring.

hidden_facts.fact: The operators involved joined in the last eight months.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks who was involved, how experienced they are, or whether it is all operators.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: Mostly recent hires. We expanded fast for Line 4. The veterans stayed on the old lines. Of course they did.

hidden_facts.fact: The experienced operator-trainer who did hands-on coaching left last year; since then new hires are qualified by read-and-sign only.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks how operators are trained or qualified on the line, or what changed in onboarding.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: We had Luc. Luc trained everyone at the glove port. Luc retired in March. Since then... they read the SOP and sign.

hidden_facts.fact: The intervention SOP was rewritten after the last inspection and is now 41 pages long.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks about the procedures themselves, their length, clarity or recent changes.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: After the last inspection we made the intervention SOP 'more complete'. It's 41 pages. It is very complete.

hidden_facts.fact: A training mock-up of the isolator glove ports exists in a storage room; it has never been used.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks about practice facilities, simulators, equipment or how people could practise safely.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: There's a mock-up. The supplier delivered it with the isolator. It's in room B-12, under a cover. Next to the Christmas decorations.

hidden_facts.fact: Operators involved in deviations scored above 90% on the existing SOP quizzes.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks whether the operators already did quizzes or how well they know the procedures.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: Their quiz scores are excellent. 92% on average. They know what the SOP says. Their gloves don't.

volunteered_facts: 16 deviations on aseptic interventions in the last quarter.
The CAPA owner has written 'retrain operators' as the corrective action.

constraints.budget: Internal resources; can fund a trainer role if justified.
constraints.deadline: CAPA due within a month; FAMHP inspection expected in the next six months.
constraints.audience: 140 cleanroom operators on three lines, two-shift pattern; about 35 on the isolator line.
constraints.schedule: Line time is extremely expensive; practical sessions must use the mock-up or planned downtime.
data_available: Deviation records with line, shift and operator
Training records and quiz scores in the learning management system
data_not_available: Any record of observed practical competence

dependencies.concern: Must approve any new training as GMP-valid, including observed qualification.
dependencies.if_ignored: A better training that doesn't count for the inspector.

dependencies.concern: Owns line time and the operators' schedule.
dependencies.if_ignored: No time for practice and the pilot collapses.

dependencies.concern: Any visual or simplified job aid must be a controlled document.
dependencies.if_ignored: Unofficial cheat sheets appear on the walls, which is itself a deviation.

dependencies.concern: Replacing Luc means a new operator-trainer role and pay grade.
dependencies.if_ignored: The skill gap returns with the next hiring wave.

traps: Read-and-sign completion and quiz scores, which are already high.
Counting the CAPA as closed when the training record is complete.

gold_plan.baseline: Intervention deviations per 1,000 interventions on Line 4 versus Lines 1 and 2, over the last two quarters.
gold_plan.behaviour: Observed qualification: each operator performs the critical interventions on the mock-up, checked against a short checklist by a qualified trainer.
gold_plan.leading_indicators: Share of Line 4 operators with an observed qualification; findings during routine line observations.
gold_plan.business_metric: Intervention deviations on Line 4 and environmental monitoring excursions.
gold_plan.collection: Deviation system, the observation checklist stored as a GMP training record, monthly review in the quality meeting.

concepts.conventional: Re-read and sign 23 SOPs with a quiz for all 140 operators.
concepts.solid: Targeted hands-on training for Line 4 operators on the mock-up, with an observed qualification as the GMP record, a one-page visual job aid for interventions, and a replacement for Luc's coaching role.
next_level_examples: Turn the veterans of Lines 1 and 2 into certified glove-port coaches, so the skill lives in people rather than in one retiring trainer.
Record short first-person videos of correct interventions on the mock-up as a controlled job aid, approved by QA.
Change the qualification standard itself: no operator works an intervention on Line 4 without an observed sign-off, written into the SOP.
also_valid: A short read-and-sign of the single intervention SOP can stay as part of the record, if hands-on qualification is the core.
red_flags: Read-and-sign for everyone as the answer.
Proposing anything that bypasses QA approval.

defence_objections: The inspector will ask for a training record on all 23 SOPs. 'We practised on a mock-up' is not a document.
Veterans coaching new hires? Their own lines will slow down, and my production manager will come for me personally.
Videos in a GMP environment? Every frame becomes a controlled document. Do you know how long that takes?
question_you_didnt_ask: Which line do the deviations come from?
actor_notes: Nathalie suspects read-and-sign won't work but needs a defensible CAPA; she rewards players who give her a better one that still survives an inspection.
She answers precise questions precisely and gets curt with vague ones ('could you be more specific?').
Low risk appetite: anything that sounds like it weakens documentation triggers pushback; framing it as a stronger GMP record lowers resistance.
She mentions the mock-up only when asked about practice facilities, with mild embarrassment.
flavour_lines: Our SOPs are so thorough that SOP-001 explains how to read SOPs.
Everyone has read the procedure. That's what their signatures say.
